newsitem.title: USA: Cerner missed out on new top-line growth.
newsitem.headline: Cerner missed out on new top-line growth.

text.p: Cerner Corp said its 1996 earnings were disappointing because it did not generate enough new top-line business and because of its need to invest heavily in the next generation of its Healthcare Network Architecture information (HNA 500) system.
Last year the company also put in motion a series of strategic alternatives it said were essential to the long-term positioning and profitable development of Cerner.

"We reorganized and restructured our sales force and substantially increased its size," said president Clifford Illig in a statement. "We also allocated increased resources to training and new marketing and communications programs," he said.

"As we complete its rollout in 1997, we believe that HNA 500 will be the most comprehensive and advanced information system solution ever developed for healthcare and believe it will substantially strengthen Cerner's competitive advantage," Illig said.

He added, "We ended the quarter with a total revenue backlog of $217.6 million, up 26.5 percent, with $110.3 million recorded as contract backlog and $107.3 million recorded as support backlog. Total revenue backlog was $172.0 million at the end of 1995."

Earlier, the clinical and management information systems developer reported fourth-quarter earnings of $0.05 a share compared with $0.25 a year ago. Quarterly revenues declined to $46.4 million from $53.0 million.
Full-year per-share earnings fell to $0.25 from $0.72.
